WHY. `clip_output` is the only thing between a failing acceptance run and the executor that has to fix it: its result is the error context a regeneration is given, capped at 4000 characters. Today the function keeps the first quarter and the last three quarters of the log and drops the middle. Measured on a real run: the dropped middle held the line `intent must be one of ...`, which was the entire diagnosis. The card burned all three attempts on a cause it was never shown, and two dependent cards were skipped behind it. A clipper that can drop the one line naming the cause is the defect; the budget is not.

WHAT YOU CHANGE. Only `clip_output` and the module-level constants it reads, inside `cards/acceptance.py`. `_OUTPUT_TAIL_CAP` stays 4000 and `_ELISION_TEMPLATE` keeps its exact text. Everything else in that file -- `run_acceptance`, `verify_card`, the stale-bytecode guard, every docstring and every comment -- comes back byte for byte as you received it. Preserve all existing docstrings and comments verbatim: this file's prose is load-bearing and it is checked.

THE NEW CONTRACT of `clip_output(text)`:

1. Text at or under the cap is returned unchanged.
2. A longer text produces a result of at most `_OUTPUT_TAIL_CAP` characters.
3. LINE ALIGNED. Every line of the result is either an elision marker line or a whole line of the input; a cut never lands inside a line. One exception, which you document and pin with a test: an input whose single line is itself longer than the cap has nothing whole to keep, and a partial line is the honest answer there.
4. The head of the log and its tail are both still kept, as today.
5. NEW, and the point of this card: the DIAGNOSIS lines of the elided middle are rescued instead of dropped. A diagnosis line is a line carrying any marker from a new module-level constant -- a tuple, named and docstringed so a reader can see and extend it -- holding at least `Error`, `error:`, `assert`, `FAILED`, `Traceback`, and the pytest `E ` line prefix. Rescued lines keep their input order, and they are filled BEFORE the tail spends the rest of the budget: the line naming the cause is worth more than the fortieth line of a summary.
6. Every gap between two kept parts is named by exactly one elision marker built from `_ELISION_TEMPLATE`, and the number it carries is EXACT: the count of input characters dropped in that gap. Several gaps mean several markers.
7. Therefore the result is `part_1 + marker_1 + part_2 + ... + part_n`, where every `part_i` is a contiguous substring of the input, and a walk of the input that adds `len(part_i)` for each part and the number `marker_i` names for each marker ends exactly at `len(text)`. This is what makes "the marker names the exact number of dropped characters" a fact rather than a wish, and it is the property your tests must check literally, by performing that walk.

- `BudgetExceeded(Exception)`: built from the limit's name, what it allowed and what was reached, carrying them as `.limit` (exactly one of the three field names above), `.allowed`, `.reached`, and `.reason` -- one short sentence naming the limit AND both numbers, fit to be copied straight into a card outcome's `reason` field. `str(exc)` is that same sentence.

  - `elapsed` -- a property: seconds since construction, by the injected clock.

THE TESTS -- `unittest`, a fake clock, no sleeping, no subprocess, no network.
